---
title: Packaging standards
department: logistics
status: current
---
Packaging standards exist to survive the conveyor, not the customer's shelf. A
parcel that looks presentable but collapses under a stack of totes will generate
a damage claim, and damage claims are the most expensive kind of incident
Northwind handles.

Every parcel must use a double wall corrugated carton rated to at least 32 ECT
when the gross weight exceeds five kilograms. Single wall cartons are acceptable
below that weight provided the contents do not shift when the carton is inverted
and shaken. Void fill must occupy at least eighty percent of the empty volume.

Pallets must be shrink wrapped with a minimum of four full turns at the base and
must not overhang the pallet edge by more than two centimetres. Overhanging
freight is the leading cause of damage in transit on the linehaul network, and a
depot may refuse to load a pallet that overhangs.

Fragile goods require a corner protector on all four vertical edges and a
fragile label on two adjacent faces. A fragile label on one face only is treated
as no label at all, because the parcel will be handled in whatever orientation
the conveyor delivers it.

Lithium batteries shipped with equipment must be declared even when the state of
charge is below thirty percent. An undeclared battery is a regulatory incident,
not a packaging defect, and the escalation window for it is much shorter.

Reusable totes are the preferred packaging for intra-network movements. Totes
must be returned on the next inbound linehaul; a depot holding more than two
hundred unreturned totes will be flagged in the weekly operations review.
